title: H3010 (125th General Assembly): Firearms criminal background checks

provenance.fetched_by: LegiScan bulk data (gun-policy Stage 5, South Carolina); operative text read by a Sonnet fill agent from the official South Carolina text (Introduced, 2022-12-08; official copy, https://www.scstatehouse.gov/sess125_2023-2024/prever/3010_20221208.htm (LegiScan doc 2617271))
provenance.note: Introduced 2022-12-08. Exempts sales by licensed dealers acting under their federal license and transfers between immediate family. Records are exempt from the Freedom of Information Act (Section 23-31-100(B)), which is part of the gun rule. Passage vote: none listed; introduced text only.

operative_text:
Section 1 (new Section 23-31-80): (B) Before any sale, exchange, or transfer pursuant to the provisions of this article, a national instant criminal background check pursuant to 18 U.S.C. Section 922 must be completed by a licensed dealer who consents to conduct the check, and upon completion of the background check, shall complete a document, the form of which shall be approved by the Chief of the State Law Enforcement Division (SLED), that identifies and confirms that the check was performed.
Section 1 (new Section 23-31-90): (A) A national instant criminal background check must be conducted and a person may not sell, exchange, or transfer a firearm at a gun show in this State except in accordance with the provisions of 18 U.S.C. 922 and the provisions of this section.
Section 1 (new Section 23-31-90): (3) If any part of a firearm transaction takes place at a gun show, no firearm may be sold, exchanged, or transferred unless a national instant background check has been obtained by a licensed gun dealer.
Section 1 (new Section 23-31-100): (A) A dealer may require that any sale, exchange, or transfer conducted pursuant to this article be subject to a fee of not more than twenty-five dollars per transaction.
Section 1 (new Section 23-31-100): (C) A person who knowingly violates the provisions of this article is guilty of a misdemeanor and, upon conviction, must be fined not more than one thousand dollars or imprisoned for not more than one year.
